title: Dissection and Isolation of Region-Specific Decellularized Lung Tissue
protocol: Setup all necessary equipment required for the dissection procedure, including a glass casserole dish, two pairs of surgical tweezers, one pair of forceps, and one pair of surgical scissors.
Autoclave the equipment before use.
Obtain a section of the lung.
Place the lung section in the glass casserole dish.
Orient the lung so that the superior end of the airway can be seen clearly.
Identify the proximal end of the vasculature.
Keep the proximal end of the vasculature intact until later steps.
Remove any pleura lining the exterior of the lung using tweezers and surgical scissors.
Expose additional airway using a spreading technique with surgical scissors.
Locate the largest airway, typically having a diameter of 2-4 cm.
Palpate down the length of the airway to determine the location of an unseen airway to a depth of approximately 1 inch.
Hold the surgical scissors parallel to the airway and insert closed tips into the tissue directly surrounding the unseen airway.
Slowly open the surgical scissors to gently pull apart the surrounding membrane without cutting any tissue.
Repeat this process intermittently throughout the dissection procedure to continue exposing the airway.
Cut the airway at branching points using surgical scissors.
Dissect along either branch independently.
Sever regions of the airway once confident that the intact ends will remain identifiable and easily located for further dissection.
Place severed regions of the airway into the corresponding tube.
Apply gentle pressure to the vasculature and slowly pull away from the airway.
Use surgical scissors to separate the vasculature from the airway.
Expose branching points in the vascular tree using surgical scissors and tweezers.
Insert closed tips of the surgical scissors just below a branching point between two corresponding vasculature regions.
Slowly open the scissors to spread apart the underlying tissues.
Remove tissue that was spread apart using the surgical scissors with a pair of tweezers.
Cut the vasculature at a branching point when it covers regions of the airway or complicates dissection.
Dissect along either branch independently after cutting the vasculature.
Sever regions of the vasculature once confident that the intact ends will remain identifiable for further dissection.
Pinch and gently tear away small regions of alveolar tissue using a pair of forceps or tweezers.
Locate a region of tissue not in the direct vicinity of the airway or the vasculature.
Pinch a small region of the tissue that appears to be devoid of any vasculature or airway.
Tear the pinched region of the tissue from the lung using the tweezers.
Observe the region of tissue removed and confirm whether it is alveolar tissue.
